breadth.label: Percent of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
breadth.note: Below 30 bullish, above 70 bearish. Computed by Thaddeus from Yahoo Finance daily closes for 502 of 503 current S&P 500 constituents at the Oct. 22 close (mimics MMFI).

markets.summary: A sharp AI selloff hit tech while most of the market held up: the Nasdaq fell 2.6% to 26,008.86, its worst day since June, and the S&P 500 lost 1.21% to 7,663.43 after Meta's huge new spending commitments and Lam Research's results revived doubts about AI costs, with the Philadelphia chip index down 6.7% and NVDA off 4.4%. The Dow eked out a 0.02% gain to 52,867.98, and breadth actually improved to 60.6% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average from 55.2%, since the majority of stocks rose. Small caps held steady, with the Russell 2000 up 0.11% to 2,784. Investors piled into Treasurys, pushing the 10-year yield down nearly 0.2 percentage point to 4.95%, below 5% for the first time in nearly a month. Gold futures fell 2.2% to $4,060.40 and silver dropped 4.6% to $54.76; both remain below their 40-week averages.

stories.headline: SpaceX falls 9% as AI spending and Tesla merger worries weigh

stories.headline: Why SpaceX stock dropped on Thursday
stories.summary: The Motley Fool points to more than $16 billion in Q3 capital spending with $35 to $40 billion projected for Q4, plus a Reuters report that some involved in the Tesla talks worry a merger could draw scrutiny and delays.

stories.headline: Nvidia slides 4.4% as revived AI doubts spark a tech selloff
stories.summary: Nvidia fell to $212.21 amid a broad chip selloff, and CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC that capital for the AI buildout, especially among smaller neocloud companies, is becoming scarce.

headlines.headline: Steep bill for AI buildout punishes Meta and other tech favorites

weather.summary: A deep upper low over California is pulling tropical moisture north, so flash flooding and severe storms are likely across the Four Corners and parts of the Southwest into Friday morning, with that threat sliding east into New Mexico and the Southern Plains over the next two days. A new low forming over the Northern High Plains sends a strong cold front down the Rockies late Friday, turning rain to a few inches of snow in the Northern Rockies under Winter Weather Advisories. As the front sweeps across the Heartland this weekend, temperatures could drop 20 to 25 degrees and end the unusually warm stretch.
